On any commodity whose declared unit is the MINORITY label among its own sized cells the reference is inverted: the guard exonerates the cells that really are divided in the wrong currency and hard-fails the one cell that is right. Measured on comparison-2026-09-02, 13 of the board's weight/volume commodities are in that shape - banana-peppers, beef-broth, chicken-broth, coconut-oil, egg-whites, evaporated-milk, honey-mustard, miracle-whip, oyster-sauce, pickles, relish, teriyaki-sauce, vegetable-broth - and on those rows the gate verdict is decided by a label tally that any single cell swap can flip, which is exactly what happened today. None of those four holds a crown, so no reader-facing price is wrong today.

items.subject: Recipe card widget charges for covered_by lines the card says you already bought
evidence: THE WHOLE POPULATION IS TWO LINES. meal-prep/db/costed.json carries exactly 2 lines with a non-empty covered_by across the entire 583-recipe catalogue: street-corn-chicken-rice-bowls / 'Lime Zest' covered_by 'Fresh Lime Juice' (grams 11, util_cost 0.69, buy_n null, pkg null, pkg_g null), and no-boil-chicken-pasta-casserole-with-artichokes-and-peas / 'Lemon Zest' covered_by 'Fresh Lemon Juice' (grams 5, util_cost 0.42, buy_n null, pkg null, pkg_g null). That is the same 2 that compute-v2 -CrossCheck reports as its 2 total disagreements.

THE LIVE NUMBERS RECONCILE EXACTLY against the feed the edge is actually serving (git show HEAD:public/smp-feed.json, generated 2026-09-02T14:56:36). pricing_inputs.limes.stores: Baker's perUnitMicros 690000, packageBasisUnits 1, purchasePriceMinor 69. costAt computes cost = purchasePriceMinor * k / 100, so k=3 gives 69*3/100 = $2.07 - the exact figure the round-2 measurement read live off street-corn-chicken-rice-bowls for a line whose own cost prose reads 'From the limes you already bought'. pricing_inputs.lemons.stores: Baker's purchasePriceMinor 85, so k=1 gives 85/100 = $0.85 - the exact figure read live off no-boil-chicken-pasta-casserole for Lemon Zest. Both claims in the queue body are therefore arithmetically confirmed, not taken on trust.

THE MECHANISM, from the code. build-card2.ps1:205-207 sets n=0, lbl empty and pkg_g=0 for a covered line, and its comment states the contract it is relying on: 'The widget already guards its buy maths on pkg_g>0 and gpu>0, so emitting 0 makes it show the ingredient and skip the purchase'. tpl2-scaler-prefix.html:301-305 pkgBasis(it,source) is: var b=Number(source.packageBasisUnits)||0; if(b>0) return b; return (it.pkg_g>0 and it.gpu>0)?(it.pkg_g/it.gpu):0. The pkg_g test is only on the SECOND line. Wherever the feed carries a packageBasisUnits - which it does for limes and lemons, both 1 - pkgBasis returns it and never looks at pkg_g at all, so k = max(1, ceil(required/packageBasis - 0.02)) >= 1 and the line is charged.

build-card2.ps1:218-220 deliberately keeps gpu INTACT on a covered line ('the widget reads gpu>0 to decide a line is priceable at all, so zeroing it would make costAt return null, and ONE null line marks the whole receipt incomplete'), so pkg_g=0 is the ONLY covered signal that reaches the browser. There is no covered flag in the data block.

pkg_g<=0 IS EXACTLY EQUIVALENT TO COVERED, and this is the load-bearing fact for the fix: build-card2.ps1:207 THROWS ('no whole-package data for ...') for any NON-covered line whose pkg_g is null or <=0. So every card that exists was built with pkg_g>0 on every non-covered line, and a pkg_g<=0 line in a data block cannot be anything but a covered line.

THE SECOND SURFACE IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT WITH THE SAME SYMPTOM. meal-prep/planner-data.js carries {"i":"Lemon Zest","g":5,"b":"2 1/3 tsp finely grated (zest of the same lemons)","bid":"lemons","gpu":6,"pk":6,"pl":"lemon"} - pk=6, not 0. Measured over the whole file: ZERO occurrences of "pk":0. The Meal Plan Builder's own pricing is CORRECT (site/tools/meal-plan-builder-tool.html:272 pkgN(it) returns null when it.pk<=0, and 286 costs n*it.pk*ppg from the item's own pk, never the feed basis), so the Builder charges the covered line because its DATA never said the line was covered. gen-planner-data.ps1 has zero occurrences of covered_by: line 72 skips a costed line whose pkg_g is null or <=0 when building costedPkg, and then Resolve-PlannerPkg (line 143) falls back to the per-ingredient catalogue at lines 51-52 (db/ingredients.json buy_pkg_g), which re-supplies the very package the suppression removed.

SURFACES AUDITED FOR covered_by, all four code readers plus the two data files: meal-prep/engine/cost-recipes.ps1 (AUTHORS covered_by, lines 274-320, and already refuses to suppress the buy when covered_by names a non-ingredient or resolves to a different bid - correct), meal-prep/pipeline/compute-v2-perserving.ps1:82 (returns null for a covered line, correct, and this is the reference implementation whose -CrossCheck is failing closed), meal-prep/pipeline/cost-render-lib.ps1:171-182 (renders the 'From the N limes you already bought' prose, correct), meal-prep/pipeline/build-card2.ps1:205 (emits the pkg_g=0 signal, correct). The two DEVIANTS are the card widget's pkgBasis and gen-planner-data.ps1. The per-serving manifest (meal-prep/pipeline/v2-perserving.json) comes from compute-v2 and is therefore already right.

surface_fix.what: honour the covered signal BEFORE the feed basis is read, in the one function everything that prices a cell already goes through. costAt is the single copy of the per-store package-cost rule since 2026-08-15 (its own comment says so), so the card widget, the store picker, cheapestAcross and priceAtStores all inherit this in one edit.
surface_fix.exact_change: pkgBasis(it,source): insert `if(!(it.pkg_g>0)) return 0;` as the FIRST statement, above the packageBasisUnits read. Safe and exactly equivalent to a covered flag because build-card2.ps1:207 throws for any non-covered line with pkg_g<=0. Then in costAt, the existing `(packageBasis>0 and k>0)` guards already make k=0 and cost=0 for that line - VERIFY that the returned cost is 0 and not null, because null marks the whole receipt incomplete (build-card2.ps1:218 names that failure mode). If it returns null, return {cost:0,k:0,up:up,variable:false,packageBasis:0} explicitly for the pkg_g<=0 case.

evidence: THE QUEUE COUNT IS FALSIFIED. The body claims '13 semicolon labels on 5 recipes plus juice of labels on 2 more'. Measured over ALL 7,838 buy labels on all 583 recipes in meal-prep/recipes-db.json (ingredients[].buy), replaying scaleBuy's own three regexes and its smpBareNum parenthesis walker: 71 labels on 36 recipes take the plain leading-number path AND carry a second bare quantity outside parentheses, plus 14 labels on 9 recipes that NO path matches at all. CLASS A - second portion, MUST scale, 55 labels. Today only the leading quantity moves. Examples verbatim: [slow-cooker-chicken-cacciatore-pasta] Balsamic Vinegar :: '1 tbsp + 1/2 tsp'; [salisbury-steak-potato-bowls] Worcestershire Sauce :: '1 tsp (patties) + 1/2 tsp (gravy)'; [garlic-butter-steak-bites-zucchini] Butter :: '1 cup plus 5 tbsp salted (2 sticks plus 5 tbsp)'; [honey-bbq-chicken-mac-and-cheese] Salt :: '3 1/2 teaspoons for the chicken; 3 1/2 teaspoons for the cheese sauce; 3 1/2 teaspoons for the pasta water (10 1/2 teaspoons total)'; [flank-steak-parmesan-green-beans] Soy Sauce :: '3/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons'.
CLASS B - range, both endpoints must scale, 2 labels. [beef-picadillo-rice-bowls] Salt :: '1/8 to 1/2 tsp fine salt'.

CLASS C - the second number MUST NOT SCALE, 14 labels, and these behave CORRECTLY today. This is the whole risk of the item and it is why a scale-every-number fix is not acceptable. Knife cuts: [country-captain-chicken] Bacon :: '9 thick-cut slices, cut into 1/2-inch pieces'; [street-corn-chicken-rice-bowls] Chicken Breast :: '4 3/4 lb, cut into 1-inch chunks'; [italian-chicken-tortellini-skillet] Chicken Breast :: '3 1/2 lb, cut into 1/2-inch pieces (about 7 breasts)'. Package-size restatements: [turkey-zucchini-noodle-casserole] Diced Tomatoes :: '3 1/2 14-oz cans, undrained (about 5 3/4 cups)' and Tomato Sauce :: '3 1/2 8-oz cans (about 3 1/4 cups)'. Per-unit restatement: [chimichurri-steak-sheet-pan] Sweet Potatoes :: '9 1/4 sweet potatoes, about 1/2 lb each'. Product-name fraction: [stuffed-chicken-breast] :: '14 oz. 1/3-less-fat cream cheese, softened'. Cook time: [sheet-pan-smoked-sausage-broccoli-cheddar] Cheddar :: '3 1/2 cups shredded cheddar, added the last 2 minutes'.

FROZEN LABELS, 14 on 9 recipes, that no path matches so nothing scales while grams do. FOUR of them MUST scale and are the queue's actual complaint: [street-corn-chicken-rice-bowls] Fresh Lime Juice :: 'juice of 3 1/2 limes; 7 tablespoons' and Lime Zest :: 'zest of 3 1/2 limes; 3 1/2 teaspoons'; [chicken-piccata-skillet] Lemon Juice :: 'juice of 3 1/2 lemons (about 2/3 cup)'; [slow-cooker-chicken-tortilla-soup-bowls] Lime Juice :: 'juice of 1 lime'. Note the shape: 'juice of 3 1/2 limes; 7 tablespoons' is ONE amount stated twice, not two portions summed, so both numbers scale by the same factor and are not added. The remaining TEN are to-taste and for-frying labels ('to taste (about 1 tsp)', 'for frying (~1 tbsp)', 'About 1 tablespoon salt and 1 1/2 teaspoons black pepper, to taste') which are CORRECTLY frozen by the 2026-09-01 decision and must stay frozen.

WHY THE JUICE-OF LABELS ARE STUCK, from the code. tpl2-scaler-prefix.html:203 SMPLEAD is a closed hedge list and its own comment says 'NOT to taste, NOT juice of, NOT for frying: each of those introduces a number that is a restatement or a garnish rather than the amount the reader measures out'. SMPRE_LEAD is anchored at ^, so 'juice of 3 1/2 limes' matches neither path and freezes. That 2026-09-01 judgement is WRONG for these four rows specifically: 'juice of 3 1/2 limes' is the recipe's only statement of the lime amount, its gram figure (210 g) doubles at 28 servings, and the reader is shown a doubled weight beside a literal 3 1/2 limes.

WHY THE SEMICOLON LABELS ARE HALF-SCALED, from the code. The 2026-09-01 fix added the two-quantity refusal to SMPRE_QUAL only ('the qualified path additionally REFUSES any label carrying a second bare quantity outside parentheses'). SMPRE_LEAD, the plain leading-number path, got no such treatment and was documented as 'deliberately unchanged'. So a label that starts with its number scales that number and leaves the second one literal - the exact half-move the 09-01 note called worse than moving neither, on the one path it did not touch.

surface_fix.what: extend the EXISTING 2026-09-01 compound-quantity rule rather than writing a second copy of it (two-copies-of-a-rule). Two additions, both narrow and both measured. (1) A CONNECTOR path: a leading quantity followed by a plus sign, the word plus, or a semicolon, followed by another quantity that carries a unit from a closed cook-unit list, is ONE amount in parts - scale every part. (2) Add 'juice of' and 'zest of' to the lead-prefix set for the LEAD path only, so those four labels scale their quantity. Everything else keeps today's behaviour byte for byte.
surface_fix.exact_change: tpl2-scaler-prefix.html: add SMPCONN = the closed connector set (plus sign, the word plus, semicolon) and SMPUNIT = the closed cook-unit list (tsp, teaspoons, tbsp, tablespoons, cups, oz, ounces, lbs, pounds, cloves, slices, sticks, cans, g, ml); add SMPRE_CONN matching leading quantity + optional unit + connector + quantity + REQUIRED SMPUNIT, tried AFTER SMPRE_LBOZ and BEFORE SMPRE_LEAD, scaling every captured quantity and re-rendering each through fmtCook; extend SMPLEAD-equivalent prefixes for SMPRE_LEAD only with 'juice of' and 'zest of'. Mirror both constants verbatim into cook-measure-lib.ps1 (CM_SB_LEAD lives there and audit-twin-drift compares the two copies on every push) and register the two new constants in ops/twin-rules.json so the twin comparison actually covers them - a new token added on one side only is the token-added-sweep-and-gate-not class.

items.root_cause: The 2026-09-01 compound-quantity fix installed 'a label is one quantity, however many numbers it takes to write it' on TWO of scaleBuy's three paths and left the third, the plain leading-number path, explicitly unchanged. So the estate has the rule and the counter-example living in the same function. Underneath that is the harder issue: a buy label is free prose and 'the number after the first one' is four different things (a second portion to add, a range endpoint, a restatement of the same amount in another unit, and a fact about the world that must never move - a knife cut, a can size, a per-unit weight, a cook time). The only sound discriminator available in the string is the CONNECTOR plus the UNIT, which is why the fix is a closed connector list and a closed unit list rather than a general multi-number scaler. Measured: 14 of the 71 multi-quantity labels are in the must-not-move set and a general scaler corrupts every one of them.
items.root_fix_note: The surface_fix IS the root fix: it extends the one shared rule and its twin, rather than adding a second parser. What it deliberately does NOT do is make the label prose unambiguous - that is repair-range-buy's job, as the 2026-09-01 note already says, and it is the right home for the 10 to-taste labels and for the (10 1/2 teaspoons total) parentheticals that stay frozen.

items.subject: smp-feed edge did not pick up today's push - 2026-09-03
evidence: THE ALERT'S PREMISE IS FALSE AND THE ORCHESTRATOR ALREADY FALSIFIED IT AT 09:55. A cache-busted fetch of https://feed.thriftycrew.com/smp-feed.json?triagecheck=<guid> returns generated 2026-09-02T14:56:36. git show HEAD:public/smp-feed.json returns generated 2026-09-02T14:56:36 - IDENTICAL. The last commit touching public/smp-feed.json is 06d75743 at 2026-09-02 14:56:37. So the edge is serving the newest PUSHED feed correctly and there is no Cloudflare problem. Do not re-diagnose Cloudflare.
The 2026-09-03T08:06:59 feed exists ONLY as an uncommitted working-tree file (git status shows ' M public/smp-feed.json'). The alert compared the edge against THAT file.

THE STALENESS IS A CONSEQUENCE OF 2026-09-03-83b57e, and the chain says so itself. capture-run.ps1:657 sets shipServed = runDownstream AND verdictSeen AND (NOT guardsBlocked), and 663 stages servedPaths (which begins with 'public') only when shipServed is true. Lines 658-661 print the reason verbatim: 'publish: staging INPUTS only - guards BLOCKED this board, so public\** and the recipe files are NOT shipped. Readers keep the last good board.' The recipe lane had already regenerated the feed at 08:06:59, before guards ran at 08:08:40-08:09:15, so public/smp-feed.json was left dirty ON PURPOSE. The commit step is NOT unconditionally skipped - two daily commits went out today, 2395d84a at 07:01:22 and f73b005e at 08:24:44 - but both carried the narrow INPUT path list, not public/**.

THE REAL DEFECT, exact line. capture-run.ps1, read-after-write block: the gate is `if ($runDownstream -and $pushed)` and the comparison basis is `$repoFeed = Get-Content (Join-Path $repo 'public\smp-feed.json') -Raw`. Both halves are wrong for this case. (a) $pushed is a WHOLE-RUN flag, not a per-file fact, and line 816 sets `$pushed = $true` with the comment 'nothing to ship is not a failed ship' - so it can be true when this file was never in the commit. (b) the basis is read from the WORKING TREE, so any writer that dirties public/smp-feed.json after the staging list was built manufactures a mismatch. The alert text then asserts a conclusion it never checked: 'The push succeeded, so this is a Cloudflare deploy that has not landed.'

THE CORRECT PATTERN IS EIGHT LINES ABOVE IT IN THE SAME FILE. The served-dirty block is gated `if ($shipServed)` with its own comment: 'It runs only when the chain actually shipped ($shipServed), so a guards-blocked run - which stages inputs only, on purpose - cannot trip it.' The edge check was written before that block and never picked up the same guard. That is why served-dirty stayed silent today and the edge check cried wolf.

This is the dates-written-not-measured / could-not-run-is-not-a-failure class: the checker inferred a publish from a local artifact instead of measuring it against git, so it manufactures a false third-party accusation on EVERY held-back board, i.e. on exactly the days when a human is already busy with a real hard fail.

surface_fix.what: gate the read-after-write on the same condition as the served-dirty block that sits above it, and compare against the COMMITTED blob rather than the working tree. Two small edits in one file; no board effect, so it can ride the batch 1 commit and stop tomorrow's run repeating the alert.
surface_fix.exact_change: In the READ-AFTER-WRITE block: change the gate from `if ($runDownstream -and $pushed)` to `if ($shipServed -and $pushed)`. Change the basis from `Get-Content (Join-Path $repo 'public\smp-feed.json')` to the committed blob, `& git -C $repo show HEAD:public/smp-feed.json` (no stderr redirect - this file runs under EAP=Stop and the surrounding comments spell out why), and do the same for the public/board.json comparison in the nested block. If the committed blob cannot be read, print BLIND and send no alert: could-not-run is not a failure. Rewrite the alert body to state what it compared - the committed generated value, the commit sha it came from, and the live value - instead of asserting 'the push succeeded'.

items.root_cause: A read-after-write check that reads its own side of the comparison from a mutable local artifact instead of from the thing that was actually published, and gates itself on a run-level boolean that is true even when there was nothing to ship. Structurally: the estate has a correct predicate for 'the chain really shipped the served files' ($shipServed, computed from the chain's own written verdict file rather than inferred from a log) and this block does not use it, so a deliberately held-back publish is indistinguishable from a failed deploy. The blast radius of that inversion is one false alert per guards-blocked day, aimed at a third party, on the day the operator can least afford a wrong lead.
items.root_fix_note: The surface_fix IS the root fix: it replaces the inferred premise with a measured one at the only site that holds it. The generalisable rule worth writing into the file's comment: any read-after-write in this chain compares against git, never against the working tree, and gates on $shipServed, never on $pushed.

WHY IT IS A LEGITIMATE SUBSET AND DOES NOT BLIND THE HARNESS: audit-food-category.ps1 never branches on store. Its only uses of the store field are the allowlist key comparison at line 91 and the report text at lines 93 and 120; the class decision at line 67 onward keys on commodity id plus the item NAME against the category-exclude library. items.root_cause: A commodity whose defining phrase is a GLOBAL_EXCLUDE token, with no relax_global to release it. GLOBAL_EXCLUDE exists to keep prepared foods out of staple commodities and '\bsauce\b' plus '\bcanned\b' are correct tokens for that job; the mechanism that makes them safe is per-commodity relax_global, and chili-beans never got one. So the rule silently disarms for the majority of its own market while looking perfectly healthy on the board, and the coverage sweep can only see the fraction of it that the include pattern ALSO misses. That is why the alert said 1 and the truth is 57: the semantic sweep asks 'does any include match', which is the wrong question when a global fence is what blocks the name - the include DOES match on 20-odd of them. The estate has the same class recorded twice already: carve-out-inherits-its-killer (a cloned commodity inheriting the exclude that kills it) and rules-that-silently-disarm.

root_fix.what: make the class visible instead of waiting for a semantic sweep to notice one instance of it. audit-coverage-gaps / explain-coverage-gap already distinguish NO-INCLUDE, EXCLUDED, CLAIMED and MATCHES; add the estate-wide sweep that asks the inverse question: for each commodity, how many corpus names does its include array MATCH and then lose to a global exclude the commodity does not relax? A commodity whose include matches many names and routes none of them is a disarmed rule, and today chili-beans would have topped that list at 20-plus.
root_fix.exact_change: Add a GLOBAL-FENCED counter per commodity: names where the commodity's include matches AND a GLOBAL_EXCLUDE pattern hits the raw name AND that pattern is absent from the commodity's relax_global. Report the top offenders with counts and the blocking token. Advisory only, no gate, and it must run on the SAME corpus the routing sim used so the two numbers are comparable.

items.root_cause: The stall is at the one stage that is a human or agent dispatch rather than a script, so it is the only stage that cannot be retried by re-running the pipeline; every automated stage in this batch completed inside twelve minutes. batch-ledger already detects and reports the condition correctly (it fired this alert 26 hours later), and it already refuses to let a batch close without the stage. What it cannot do is make the dispatch happen, so a batch whose orchestrator ends between publish and review sits open until an alert catches it. On 2026-09-02 the orchestrator that opened this wave was the one whose plan round bounced two findings (corn05 and corn06) - the review was the next step and the round ended first.
items.root_fix_note: No code fix is warranted from one instance: the detector works, the close gate works, and the alert arrived. What is worth booking rather than building is whether wave-publish should refuse to return until the review is dispatched, or whether the alert cadence should be hours rather than 26 - see deferred_findings. Do not build either from a single data point.

deferred_findings.what: Arm audit-unit-basis-outlier's measure-kind gate on the row's DECLARED unit instead of the peer label majority, after adjudicating the 11 crown cells it newly arms. Measured today: 13 commodities are in the inverted-reference shape and the switch takes the gate from hard=1 to hard=11 on day one. All 11 are enumerated with item names, sizes and prices in plan-2026-09-03.routing.json basis_kind_measurement.crown_findings_unit_reference: banana-peppers/Walmart 32 fl oz, beef-broth/Aldi 32 oz, chicken-broth/Aldi 32 oz (the item name itself says 32 FL OZ), coconut-oil/Sam's Club 128 fl oz, egg-whites/Aldi 32 oz (item name says 32 FL OZ), evaporated-milk/Walmart 12 fl oz, honey-mustard/Sam's Club 128 fl oz, miracle-whip/Aldi 30 fl oz, oyster-sauce/Fareway 12.6 oz, relish/Aldi 16 fl oz, vegetable-broth/Walmart 31.8 oz. Several are the trivial same-number-two-labels case where the ITEM NAME states the true kind while the size field's label does not, which suggests a cheaper root fix than 11 allowlist entries: read the kind off the product name when it states a size, and fall back to the size field's label.

check-ad-cycles.ps1:2634 writes test-guards-weekly-stamp.txt on FAILURE as well as success, by an explicit decision (one alert per week, not one per day). The consequence is that nothing in the estate can measure how long it has been since a hard invariant was actually PROVEN: rc=3 on 2026-08-27 and again on 2026-09-03, last pass 2026-08-20, and the stamp today reads 2026-09-03. Cheapest honest fix: a second stamp file written only on rc=0, plus an advisory warn when it exceeds 14 days. This is the gates-that-can-never-arm shape and it is one line of consequence, not a redesign.

frozen-vegetables (index 97) has a bare include 'mixed\s+vegetables' with no frozen requirement, so it claims every mixed-vegetable name ahead of canned-mixed-vegetables (index 353). Measured: 57 corpus names route to frozen-vegetables and 9 carry no frozen signal at all, including 'Green Mountain Coffee Roasters Vermont Country Blend Medium Roast K-Cup Coffee Pods' via the include '(?:california|normandy|winter|italian|garden|country)\s+blend'. The coffee holds no cell today (frozen-vegetables' crown is Hy-Vee at 0.0783) so nothing published is wrong, but a produce commodity that can claim a K-Cup is a live hijack risk. Needs its own measured routing pass with cell_effects for all 6 frozen-vegetables cells, on a day the board is not already held back. Full 9-name list in this plan's item 7423a0 evidence.

The coverage ledger carries audit-ff-carry at tolerance 100 percent ('examined 60 of 595 eligible (baseline 464, tol 100%)'), which sets the floor at zero, so that ratchet can never fire however far the re-probe count collapses. Arguably unfixable as written, because the examined count legitimately swings with how many terms the pull already covers (467 skipped today). If it is to mean anything the metric has to change, not the tolerance - e.g. ratchet on (re-probed + already-covered) against the term list, or on the THROTTLED count, which was 68 today. Also worth asking in the same pass: should the Freshop recovery pass run in a LATER window rather than more slowly in the same throttled one - the cadence-not-pacing shape.

post-publish-review is the only REQUIRED batch stage that is an agent dispatch rather than a script, so it is the only one a stopped orchestrator can leave undone, and the alert took 26 hours to notice. Two candidate answers, neither worth building from one instance: wave-publish refuses to return until the review is dispatched, or the stale-batch alert cadence drops from daily to hours for batches that have stamped publish. Revisit if it happens twice.

open_questions_for_brad.question: Does chili-beans mean any bean in a chili sauce, or pinto/red beans specifically? The fix admits 57 products, and among them are white/great-northern rows ('Bush's Best Great Northern Beans Mild Chili Sauce White Chili Beans 15.5 Oz', 'Bush's Chili Magic Beans, Slow Simmered White Beans in Mild Chili Sauce', 'Mrs. Grimes White Chili Beans in Chili Sauce'), a black-bean row, and two Chili Magic rows which Bush's markets as a chili STARTER rather than a side.
open_questions_for_brad.why_not_blocking: The plan rules them IN on the evidence: the commodity's label is 'Chili Beans (in sauce)' with no bean-type qualifier, its existing include is bean-type agnostic ('chili\s+(?:style\s+)?beans?'), and the semantic sweep itself scored the Chili Magic row at 0.929 as an instance of this commodity. If Brad wants pinto/red only, it is one added exclude and the routing artifact already lists every affected name, so the reversal is cheap and fully measured.
options: A: any bean in a chili sauce, including white and black and the Chili Magic starter - what the plan ships
B: pinto and red only - add an exclude for white/great-northern/black and for 'chili magic', which drops roughly 8 of the 57 names
C: split a white-chili-beans carve-out - note carve-out-inherits-its-killer: a clone would inherit the missing relax_global that caused this whole item, so it must be given relax_global explicitly

open_questions_for_brad.question: Should the board print a per-unit price at all for a commodity whose stores label the same product by weight AND by volume? Thirteen commodities are in that shape today (banana-peppers, beef-broth, chicken-broth, coconut-oil, egg-whites, evaporated-milk, honey-mustard, miracle-whip, oyster-sauce, pickles, relish, teriyaki-sauce, vegetable-broth), and on those rows the published per-unit figures are a mixture of per-weight-ounce and per-fluid-ounce numbers with no conversion. Today's stop was one symptom of it.
open_questions_for_brad.why_not_blocking: Nothing published is wrong on the row that stopped the board (teriyaki's crown is cheapest in either currency across the whole plausible density range), and the batch 1 fix is a reviewed allowlist entry that self-voids on any size change. But the underlying question is a product decision, not a code one, and it decides whether the deferred work is 11 allowlist entries, a density table, or a rule that a mixed-basis commodity shows a pack price instead of a per-unit price.
options: A: keep per-unit and adjudicate cell by cell as the guard finds them - the status quo, 12 allowlist entries so far
B: add a density table for the liquids that need one and convert properly, which makes the numbers comparable and the guard meaningful
C: for a commodity whose stores disagree on the KIND of quantity, print the package price and drop the per-unit column

no_needs_brad_item_note: No open queue id is classified needs-brad this round, and that is deliberate rather than an omission. Both questions above are confirmations of rulings this plan already makes on measured evidence, each with a one-hunk reversal and a written blast radius, so parking a real fix behind a decision would leave a wrong price live for no gain. The genuinely blocked work from earlier rounds stays parked where it is: 2026-08-31-cafc3e is needs-brad and is not re-triaged here.
